You are assembling a clinical visit note. The sentences of one note are listed below in random order with their section headings removed. File every sentence under one of these four headings: SUBJECTIVE, OBJECTIVE EXAM, OBJECTIVE RESULTS, ASSESSMENT AND PLAN. In the JSON, the headings are the keys subjective, objective_exam, objective_results and assessment_and_plan. Return each sentence ID under exactly one heading. Do not leave any sentence out and do not invent IDs.

SECTION DEFINITIONS
- SUBJECTIVE: what the patient reports and the history taken before the examination: the reason for the visit, the history of the present illness, the review of systems, past medical, surgical, family and social history, current medications and allergies.
- OBJECTIVE EXAM: what the clinician found on physical examination at this visit, including vital signs measured at the visit.
- OBJECTIVE RESULTS: results of laboratory tests, imaging and other studies that were reviewed.
- ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: the clinician's diagnoses or impressions, the reasoning behind them, treatment decisions, prescriptions, orders, referrals, patient instructions and follow-up.
A sentence goes under the heading that names its role in the note, not its topic. A symptom the patient reports belongs under SUBJECTIVE even if the plan discusses it again; a sentence that restates a symptom or finding to justify a decision belongs under ASSESSMENT AND PLAN.

For each sentence also give placement_confidence: HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW, meaning how sure you are that it belongs under that heading rather than another. If any sentence is LOW, set requires_review to true.

<sentences>
S1: We will also obtain a set of baseline labs.
S2: - Examination: Sensation intact in left lower extremity.
S3: - Patient Education and Counseling: I encouraged her to keep her appointment with ophthalmology for her diabetic eye exam.
S4: Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
S5: Patient reports history significant for type 2 diabetes and hypertension.
S6: - Medical Treatment: X-ray ordered to rule out fracture.
S7: Pain with valgus stress testing.
S8: She will start Naprosyn 500 mg twice daily for pain control.
S9: Musculoskeletal: Reports left ankle pain and swelling.\ Denies left calf pain, lower left leg pain, or left knee pain.
S10: - Auscultation of Lungs: Clear bilaterally.
S11: - Medical Treatment: We will keep her on her current dose of metformin and order a repeat hemoglobin A1c.
S12: Patient reports taking metformin and Norvasc.
S13: - Medical Reasoning: Given the nature of her injury, I believe this is an ankle sprain.
S14: - Medical Reasoning: She is doing well with Norvasc.
S15: - Examination: Pulses are normal in left lower extremity.
S16: A refill was sent for this today.
S17: - Auscultation of Heart: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, unchanged from previous exam.
S18: Continue with ice and elevation.
S19: - Patient Education and Counseling: I encouraged her to continue with home monitoring and knows to contact the office if needed.
S20: - Medical Reasoning: This appears to be well controlled with her current regimen.
S21: We will place her in an air splint and have her ambulate with crutches to avoid weightbearing until we get the x-ray results.
S22: - General Examination: No bruits.
S23: - Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient that I will contact her with the results of her x-ray, and that if these reveal a fracture, we will put in a referral to orthopedics for further evaluation.
S24: - Medical Treatment: We will keep her on her current dose of Norvasc.
S25: - Examination of the left ankle: Tender to palpation over the lateral malleolus and fifth metatarsal.
</sentences>
